name: Doorway Chest Stretch
feel: Across the front of your chest.
avoid: Twisting hard or letting the shoulder roll forward.
easier: Place the elbow below shoulder height and take a smaller step.
instructions: Stand beside a doorway. Rest one forearm against the frame, elbow slightly below shoulder height.
Step forward gently and turn your chest a little away from the supported arm.
Keep the shoulder relaxed. Hold at light tension, then change arms.
cue: Turn gently away from the arm

name: Seated Butterfly Stretch
feel: Along the inner thighs.
avoid: Pushing the knees down with your hands.
easier: Sit on a folded towel and move your feet farther from your hips.
instructions: Sit tall and bring the soles of your feet together in front of you.
Hold your ankles and let your knees fall outward under their own weight.
If comfortable, lean slightly forward from the hips. Keep your back long and breathe.
cue: Let the knees relax outward

name: Standing Quad Stretch
feel: The front of the bent-leg thigh.
avoid: Arching the back or pulling the knee far out to the side.
easier: Hold a wall and use a strap around the ankle if reaching the foot is difficult.
instructions: Stand beside a wall and hold it with one hand. Bend the other knee and hold that foot behind you.
Bring your knees near one another and gently tuck your pelvis.
Ease the heel toward your buttock without pulling hard. Stay tall, then switch legs.
cue: Knees close; keep the pelvis tucked

name: Supported Couch Stretch
feel: The front of the rear thigh and hip.
avoid: Forcing your torso upright or pressing into a painful kneecap.
easier: Use a low cushion for the rear foot, pad the knee, and keep your torso slightly forward.
instructions: Kneel on padding in front of a low couch, facing away. Rest one foot on the seat behind you.
Step the opposite foot forward and support your hands on that thigh or a chair.
Gently tuck your pelvis. Rise only as far as comfortable while keeping the back knee padded.
cue: Pad the knee; rise only a little

name: Seated Figure-4 Stretch
feel: The outer hip of the crossed leg.
avoid: Pressing on the knee or rounding the back to get lower.
easier: Keep the crossed ankle farther forward or stay upright.
instructions: Sit near the front of a sturdy chair with both feet down.
Place one ankle across the opposite thigh, just above the knee. Keep the crossed foot gently flexed.
Lean forward from your hips with a long back. Stop at light tension and change sides after the hold.
cue: Hinge forward with a long back

name: Supported Standing Figure-4
feel: The buttock and outer hip of the crossed leg.
avoid: Balancing without support or pushing the crossed knee down.
easier: Use the seated figure-4 stretch instead.
instructions: Hold a sturdy chair or rail with both hands. Cross one ankle above the other knee.
Bend the supporting knee a little and sit your hips back.
Keep the chest lifted and the crossed foot gently flexed. Hold lightly, stand up, then switch.
cue: Hold a support and sit back

name: Chair Hamstring Stretch
feel: The back of the extended thigh.
avoid: Reaching for your toes by rounding your spine.
easier: Bend the extended knee slightly and lean less.
instructions: Sit near the front of a chair. Extend one leg with its heel on the floor.
Keep a soft knee and toes facing up. Rest your hands on the bent-leg thigh.
Tip forward from the hips until the back of the straight thigh gently stretches, then switch legs.
cue: Hinge from the hips; keep a soft knee

name: Half-Split Hamstring Stretch
feel: The back of the front thigh.
avoid: Locking the front knee or collapsing your chest.
easier: Rest your hands on blocks or a chair and keep the front knee a little bent.
instructions: Start in a half-kneeling stance with one foot in front.
Shift your hips back over the kneeling leg as the front leg lengthens. Let the front toes lift.
Lean forward a little from the hips with hands supported. Hold, then ease forward and change legs.
cue: Hips back; front heel stays down

name: Adductor Rock-Back
feel: Along the inner thigh of the straight leg.
avoid: Rounding your back or forcing the hips toward the heel.
easier: Keep the sideways leg closer and make the rocking motion smaller.
instructions: Begin on hands and knees. Extend one leg straight out to the side with the foot on the floor.
Keep a long back and slowly move your hips backward.
Pause at mild inner-thigh tension, then come forward. Repeat smoothly before switching sides.
cue: Rock back slowly; keep the spine long

name: Supported Frog Stretch
feel: Across the inner thighs.
avoid: Spreading the knees too wide or forcing a deep position.
easier: Bring the knees closer together and rest on your hands instead of forearms.
instructions: Start on hands and knees on thick padding. Move your knees apart only as far as comfortable.
Bend your knees around right angles so the lower legs point backward. Support your upper body on hands or forearms.
Ease your hips backward a little. Hold at gentle tension, then bring the knees in slowly.
cue: Pad both knees; use a small range

name: 90/90 Front-Hip Stretch
feel: The outer hip of the front leg.
avoid: Pressing the knee into the floor or twisting through knee pain.
easier: Sit on a cushion and put your hands behind you for support.
instructions: Sit with one leg bent in front and the other to the side, both knees near right angles.
Face the front shin. Lengthen your back and rest your hands on the floor.
Hinge toward the front thigh a little, keeping weight through the hips. Hold, then reposition to switch sides.
cue: Lean toward the front shin

name: 90/90 Hip Switches
feel: Controlled rotation at both hips.
avoid: Forcing the knees down or moving through knee pain.
easier: Keep your hands behind you and make a smaller side-to-side movement.
instructions: Sit with knees bent, feet wider than hip width, and hands supporting you behind.
Slowly lower both knees toward one side into a comfortable 90/90 shape.
Lift both knees through the middle and lower them to the other side. Keep the movement slow.
cue: Move both knees gently side to side

name: Supported Pigeon Stretch
feel: The buttock of the front leg.
avoid: Forcing the front shin parallel or feeling twisting at the knee.
easier: Choose the lying figure-4 stretch if your knee feels uncomfortable.
instructions: From hands and knees, slide one knee forward and bring that foot across toward the opposite hip.
Extend the other leg back. Place a firm cushion beneath the front-side hip so you can stay supported.
Keep the front foot near the opposite hip and your torso upright. Hold gently without forcing the front knee.
cue: Support the hip; keep the foot close

name: Kneeling Bench Lat Stretch
feel: Along the sides of your upper back and under the arms.
avoid: Dropping into your lower back or forcing the shoulders down.
easier: Use a higher support and keep the hips closer to it.
instructions: Kneel in front of a stable chair or bench and place both hands on its seat.
Move your hips backward while keeping your hands supported and your back long.
Let your chest lower gently between your arms. Keep the ribs controlled and breathe.
cue: Sit the hips back; keep ribs controlled

name: Puppy Pose
feel: Through the shoulders and upper back.
avoid: Forcing your chest to the floor or arching your lower back.
easier: Place your forehead on a cushion and reach less far.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with hips above knees.
Walk your hands forward while keeping your hips near the same position.
Lower your forehead toward a support and ease the chest downward. Keep the lower back comfortable.
cue: Hips above knees; reach forward

name: Thread-the-Needle Stretch
feel: Around the shoulder blade and upper back of the reaching arm.
avoid: Resting your weight on your neck or forcing the twist.
easier: Slide the arm a shorter distance and keep the other hand planted.
instructions: Start on hands and knees. Slide one arm underneath your chest toward the opposite side, palm facing up.
Bend the supporting elbow a little and let the reaching shoulder lower toward the mat.
Keep hips above the knees and the head supported comfortably. Hold, return slowly, and switch arms.
cue: Reach under; keep hips over knees

name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
feel: From the back corner of the neck toward the shoulder blade.
avoid: Pulling on your head or lifting the shoulder.
easier: Make the head turn and downward nod smaller.
instructions: Sit upright and rest one hand lightly on the chair seat.
Turn your head a little away from that side, then look down toward the opposite armpit.
Let the shoulder remain heavy. Hold with no hand pressure on your head, then switch sides.
cue: Look gently toward the opposite armpit

name: Standing Wrist Extensor Stretch
feel: Along the back of the forearm.
avoid: Pulling hard on the fingers or locking the elbow.
easier: Bend the elbow a little and use very light hand pressure.
instructions: Reach one arm forward at a comfortable height with the palm facing down.
Let the wrist bend so the fingers point toward the floor.
Use the other hand to guide the back of the hand gently toward you. Keep the shoulder relaxed and switch arms after the hold.
cue: Palm down; fingers point toward floor

name: Standing Wrist Flexor Stretch
feel: Along the palm side of the forearm.
avoid: Locking your elbow or tugging hard on individual fingers.
easier: Keep a small bend in the elbow and reduce the pull.
instructions: Extend one arm forward with the palm facing up.
Let the fingers angle down and use the opposite hand to support them together.
Gently draw the hand back toward you until the forearm stretches. Keep the shoulder down, then change sides.
cue: Palm up; use only light pressure

name: Wall Biceps Stretch
feel: The front of the upper arm.
avoid: Turning too far or letting the shoulder slide forward.
easier: Lower the hand and turn away only slightly.
instructions: Stand beside a wall and rest one palm against it with the arm extended a little behind you.
Keep the elbow soft and the shoulder relaxed.
Turn your chest gently away from the wall until the front of the arm stretches. Hold and switch sides.
cue: Soft elbow; turn the chest away

name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Stretch
feel: The lower calf and a comfortable bend at the ankle.
avoid: Lifting the heel or letting the knee collapse inward.
easier: Move the toes closer to the wall.
instructions: Face a wall with one foot a short distance from it and the other foot behind for balance.
Keeping the front heel down, bend the front knee toward the wall over the middle toes.
Pause where comfortable. Move the foot closer if the heel lifts; hold and switch ankles.
cue: Heel down; knee follows the toes

name: Seated Toe and Arch Stretch
feel: Under the foot through the arch.
avoid: Yanking the toes or cramping the foot.
easier: Keep the ankle relaxed and move the toes less.
instructions: Sit in a chair and rest one ankle across the opposite thigh.
Support the heel with one hand and hold the toes together with the other.
Draw the toes gently back toward the shin until the arch lengthens. Hold lightly, then switch feet.
cue: Support the heel; ease the toes back

name: Child’s Pose Side Reach
feel: Along one side of the back and ribs.
avoid: Forcing the hips toward the heels or lifting one hip.
easier: Rest the hips on a cushion and reach less far.
instructions: From hands and knees, ease your hips back toward your heels and reach both hands forward.
Walk both hands a short distance to the right while keeping the hips heavy and level.
Breathe into the left side of your back. Return through the middle and reach left to stretch the other side.
cue: Walk the hands sideways; keep hips level

name: Wall Thoracic Rotation
feel: Easy rotation through the upper back.
avoid: Twisting the hips or pushing into shoulder pain.
easier: Keep the moving elbow bent and use a smaller turn.
instructions: Stand side-on to a wall and rest the nearer hand on it at chest height.
Reach the other arm forward, then slowly open it away from the wall as your chest follows.
Keep the hips facing ahead. Return with control and repeat before changing sides.
cue: Rotate the chest; keep hips still
